newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks set records in post-holiday rally.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks set records in post-holiday rally.

text.p: Toronto stocks enjoyed a post-holiday rally on Tuesday, shrugging off weak gold prices to set new closing and intraday records.
The TSE 300 Composite Index jumped 51.94 points to close at 6903.08, eclipsing the previous record set last Thursday.
The key index also set an intraday high of 6904.41 on Tuesday.
Canadian markets were closed on Monday for a civic holiday. Canada's biggest stock market ignored a sharp drop in gold prices to post its 32nd record close of 1997.
The TSE's heavyweight gold group sank 145 points as COMEX December gold ended down $3.50 at $324.60 an ounce.
Losses in gold and pipelines were more than offset by strong gains in communications, oil and gas, conglomerates and base metals.
"I think we're seeing some catch up from yesterday," said Jim Doak, president of Enterprise Capital Management Inc.
Toronto's trading volume totaled almost 78 million shares worth C$1.25 billion ($905 million)
Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 541 to 473, with 277 issues unchanged.
* Alcan Aluminium Ltd. closed up 1.30 at 54.90 after earlier hitting a 52-week high of 55.70.

The world's second biggest aluminum producer said on Tuesday that it settled a lawsuit against the British Columbia government over its canceled Kemano hydroelectric project and said it might build a C$1.2 billion ($870 million) smelter in the province.
* Creditor-protected Gandalf Technologies Inc. fell 0.12 to 0.28 on 857,000 shares. Toronto Stock Exchange officials said on Tuesday they were reviewing Gandalf's stock listing.
* National Trustco Inc. gained 0.35 to 34.60 after the Canadian government approved Bank of Nova Scotia's C$1.25 billion bid ($905 million) for Canada's last big family-owned trust.
Bank of Nova Scotia gained 0.35 to 65.70.
